question: As per the Hindu calendar, Ugadi festival in southern states of India is celebrated in which of the following months?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chaitra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ugadi (also called Yugadi) marks the beginning of a new lunisolar year and is celebrated on the first day of the Hindu month of Chaitra, usually falling in March-April. (उगादी — चैत्र मास)

 

• It is celebrated primarily in the southern states of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka (where it is called Ugadi), while in Maharashtra the same day is celebrated as Gudi Padwa.

 

• A characteristic ritual food of the festival is Ugadi Pachadi, a mixture of six tastes (sweet, sour, salty, bitter, tangy and spicy) symbolising the different flavours/experiences of life.

 

• The day also traditionally marks the start of the Hindu lunar calendar (Panchanga), and new Panchangas are read out in temples on this day.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Similar New Year festivals falling around the same time include Gudi Padwa (Maharashtra), Cheti Chand (Sindhi community) and Baisakhi/Vaisakhi (Punjab, though celebrated in the month of Vaishakha).

 

NOTE

 

• Margashirsha (Option 1): Corresponds to November-December in the Hindu calendar, not associated with Ugadi.

 

• Vaishaka (Option 2): Corresponds to April-May; this month is associated with festivals like Buddha Purnima and Baisakhi, not Ugadi.

 

• Shravan (Option 4): Corresponds to July-August, considered auspicious for Lord Shiva worship (Shravan somvar), not Ugadi.

question: Who among the following was the winner of the National Film Award in 2002 for his choreography in the Hindi movie ‘Lagaan’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raju Khan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raju Khan, son of veteran choreographer Saroj Khan, won the National Film Award for Best Choreography for his work in Lagaan (2001), notably for songs such as "O Rey Chhori". (राजू खान — राष्ट्रीय फिल्म पुरस्कार, लगान)

 

• Lagaan, directed by Ashutosh Gowariker and starring Aamir Khan, was a major critical and commercial success and was also nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film in 2002.

 

• The film's music was composed by A. R. Rahman, with lyrics by Javed Akhtar.

 

• The National Film Award for Best Choreography recognises outstanding dance choreography in Indian feature films and has been awarded annually since the early 1990s.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lagaan swept several other National Film Awards, including the National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment.

 

• Raju Khan has also choreographed songs for films such as Devdas and Jodhaa Akbar.

 

NOTE

 

• Ahmed Khan (Option 1): A well-known Bollywood choreographer and director, but he was not the National Award winner for Lagaan; he is better known for films like Baaghi and Heropanti.

 

• Dinesh Kumar (Option 3): Not associated with the choreography of Lagaan.

 

• Shiamak Davar (Option 4): A prominent Indian choreographer and dance instructor, but not the National Award winner for Lagaan.

question: Which of the following is a feature of public goods?
option_2: These goods are limited in supply.
option_3: Consumption of one person does not affect the consumption of another person.
option_4: Only tax payers can get the benefit of public goods.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Consumption of one person does not affect the consumption of another person.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Public goods are characterised by two key properties: non-rivalry and non-excludability. (सार्वजनिक वस्तुएँ — अप्रतिस्पर्धी उपभोग)

 

• Non-rivalry means that one person's consumption of the good does not reduce its availability for others — for example, national defence, street lighting or a public park can be "consumed" by one person without diminishing what is available to another.

 

• Non-excludability means that once the good is provided, no one can be effectively excluded from using it, even those who did not pay for it (this leads to the "free-rider problem").

 

• Because of these two features, public goods are typically provided by the government rather than private markets, which tend to under-supply them.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Goods can be classified into four types based on rivalry and excludability: private goods (rival and excludable), public goods (non-rival and non-excludable), common resources (rival but non-excludable) and club goods (non-rival but excludable).

 

• Examples of public goods include national defence, lighthouses, street lighting and clean air.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (more competitive): Incorrect — public goods are non-rivalrous, i.e. non-competitive in consumption, not more competitive.

 

• Option 2 (limited in supply): Incorrect — being "limited in supply" is not a defining feature of public goods; scarcity applies to economic goods generally, not specifically to public goods.

 

• Option 4 (only tax payers benefit): Incorrect — public goods are non-excludable, meaning even non-tax payers can benefit from them (the free-rider problem).

question: Which of the following is a right under Article 300A?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right to property.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 300A of the Indian Constitution states: "No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law." It guarantees the Right to Property. (अनुच्छेद 300A — संपत्ति का अधिकार)

 

• This provision was inserted by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, which removed the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights (it was earlier Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31) and made it a constitutional/legal right under Part XII of the Constitution.

 

• As a legal right (not a fundamental right), a violation of Article 300A can be challenged in a High Court under Article 226, but not directly in the Supreme Court under Article 32.

 

• The amendment was aimed at facilitating land reform measures by the state without being obstructed by fundamental rights litigation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 300A falls under Part XII of the Constitution, which deals with "Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits".

 

• The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 was enacted during the Janata Party government led by Morarji Desai.

 

NOTE

 

• Right to freedom (Option 1): Guaranteed under Articles 19-22 of Part III (Fundamental Rights).

 

• Right to life (Option 2): Guaranteed under Article 21 of Part III (Fundamental Rights).

 

• Right to education (Option 4): Guaranteed under Article 21A of Part III (Fundamental Rights), inserted by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

question: Which of the following is known as the world’s wettest place?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mawsynram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mawsynram, a village in the East Khasi Hills district of Meghalaya, India, is widely recorded as the wettest place on Earth, receiving an average annual rainfall of around 11,872 mm. (मॉसिनराम — विश्व का सबसे अधिक वर्षा वाला स्थान)

 

• Mawsynram surpassed the nearby town of Cherrapunji (Sohra), also in Meghalaya, which held the record earlier and still holds records for the highest rainfall in a single calendar month and a single year.

 

• The exceptionally high rainfall here is due to its location on the windward side of the Khasi Hills, which forces moisture-laden monsoon winds from the Bay of Bengal to rise sharply and condense.

 

• Meghalaya, meaning "abode of clouds", records the world's heaviest rainfall in this region due to the funnel-shaped topography that channels and lifts monsoon clouds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cherrapunji (Sohra) holds the Guinness World Record for the most rainfall in a calendar month (July 1861) and most rainfall in a year (August 1860 - July 1861).

 

• Meghalaya's capital is Shillong.

 

NOTE

 

• Waialeale (Option 1): A mountain on the island of Kauai, Hawaii, often cited as one of the wettest spots on Earth, but it does not hold the overall record ahead of Mawsynram.

 

• Mumbai (Option 2): Receives heavy monsoon rainfall but is nowhere near the wettest place in the world.

 

• Singapore (Option 4): A tropical city-state with high rainfall, but not recognised as the world's wettest place.

question: In September 2022, which legislative assembly withdrew a bill aimed at prohibiting the movement of stray cattle on roads and public places in urban areas of the state, months after it was passed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Gujarat Cattle Control (Keeping and Movement) Bill, 2022, which aimed to regulate and prohibit the free movement of stray cattle in urban areas, was withdrawn by the Gujarat Legislative Assembly in September 2022. (गुजरात मवेशी नियंत्रण विधेयक — वापस लिया गया)

 

• The bill had been passed earlier in March 2022 but faced strong protests from cattle-rearing communities (such as the Maldhari community), who felt their livelihoods would be adversely affected.

 

• Amid the protests, the Gujarat government first postponed and then, in the assembly session starting 21 September 2022, formally withdrew the bill.

 

• This happened ahead of the Gujarat Assembly elections held in December 2022.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gujarat's Chief Minister at the time was Bhupendra Patel.

 

• The bill had proposed restricting cattle movement in urban/municipal areas and mandating registration and shelters for cattle owners.

 

NOTE

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 1): Did not withdraw such a stray cattle bill in September 2022.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): Has separate cattle-related laws (like the UP Prevention of Cow Slaughter Act) but did not withdraw such a bill in this context.

 

• Assam (Option 4): Passed the Assam Cattle Preservation Act, 2021, but did not withdraw it in September 2022.

question: Who became the Nawab of Bengal in 1756 after the death of Alivardi Khan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Siraj Ud Daulah.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Siraj-ud-Daulah succeeded his maternal grandfather Alivardi Khan as the Nawab of Bengal in 1756. (सिराज उद-दौला — बंगाल का नवाब, 1756)

 

• He is best remembered for the Battle of Plassey (23 June 1757), in which he was defeated by the British East India Company forces under Robert Clive, largely due to the betrayal of his commander Mir Jafar.

 

• The defeat at Plassey marked the beginning of British political dominance in Bengal and, eventually, in India.

 

• Following the battle, Siraj-ud-Daulah was captured and executed, and Mir Jafar was installed as a puppet Nawab by the British.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Black Hole of Calcutta incident (1756) is also associated with Siraj-ud-Daulah's reign, following his capture of Fort William from the British.

 

• The Battle of Buxar (1764), fought later against a combined force of the Nawab of Awadh, the Mughal Emperor and the Nawab of Bengal (Mir Qasim), further cemented British control over Bengal, Bihar and Odisha.

 

NOTE

 

• Nigam Shaan (Option 2) and Shaan Nawab (Option 3): Not historical figures associated with the Nawabs of Bengal.

 

• Murshid Quli Khan (Option 4): Was an earlier Nawab of Bengal (from 1717), and founder of the city of Murshidabad; he predates Alivardi Khan and Siraj-ud-Daulah.

question: An early temple at Bhitargaon, Uttar Pradesh was built about 1500 years ago was made of _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is baked brick.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bhitargaon Temple, located in Kanpur Dehat district, Uttar Pradesh, is one of the earliest surviving examples of a brick temple in India, built during the Gupta period (around the 5th century CE). (भितरगांव मंदिर — पक्की ईंट)

 

• It is dedicated to Lord Vishnu and is notable for being made almost entirely of baked (fired) brick, with terracotta panels depicting scenes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranic legends.

 

• It is considered one of the tallest brick structures to have survived from the Gupta era and represents an important stage in the evolution of temple architecture in India, particularly the development of the shikhara (curvilinear spire).

 

• The temple demonstrates advanced brick-laying and corbelling techniques used to construct its pyramidal roof.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable Gupta-era temples include the Dashavatara Temple at Deogarh (made of stone) and temples at Bhumara and Nachna-Kuthara.

 

• The Gupta period (4th-6th century CE) is often referred to as the "Golden Age" of ancient India due to advances in art, architecture, science and literature.

 

NOTE

 

• Wood (Option 1): Not the material used; wood does not survive for 1500 years in the Indian climate in the way the Bhitargaon structure has.

 

• Mud brick (Option 2): Sun-dried mud brick was used in earlier and more perishable structures, not this durable Gupta-era temple.

 

• Clay and thatch (Option 3): Associated with simple huts, not a monumental Gupta temple.

question: Which of the following is a famous folk dance of Odisha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rangabati.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rangabati is a hugely popular Sambalpuri folk song and dance form from the Sambalpur region of Odisha, closely tied to the state's folk-dance tradition. (रंगबती — ओडिशा का लोकनृत्य)

 

• It originated as a Sambalpuri folk song (made famous by singers Jitendra Haripal and Krishna Patel) and became closely associated with an accompanying energetic folk dance performed at festivals and cultural events across Odisha.

 

• Odisha's rich folk-dance tradition also includes Dalkhai, Ghumura, Sambalpuri and Chhau (Mayurbhanj Chhau), but among the given options, only Rangabati is linked to Odisha.

 

• Odisha is also home to the classical dance form Odissi, one of the eight recognised classical dances of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mayurbhanj Chhau, a martial-art-based folk dance from Odisha, is performed without masks, unlike the Chhau of Purulia (West Bengal) and Seraikella (Jharkhand).

 

• Odissi dance traces its origins to temple traditions and the devadasi system associated with the Jagannath Temple, Puri.

 

NOTE

 

• Birha (Option 1): A folk song/singing style associated with Bhojpuri-speaking regions of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, not a dance of Odisha.

 

• Ghoomar (Option 2): A traditional folk dance of Rajasthan, performed by women, especially of the Bhil tribe.

 

• Kalbelia (Option 3): A folk dance of the Kalbelia (snake-charmer) community of Rajasthan, inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage.

question: Which theory discusses the relationship between ligand bonding and degradation of d orbitals in metal complexes and the geometry of metal complexes and the splitting of d orbitals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Crystal field theory (CFT).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Crystal Field Theory (CFT) explains the bonding, geometry and properties of transition metal complexes by treating the ligands as point negative charges that create an electrostatic field around the central metal ion, causing the degeneracy of the d orbitals to be lifted (split). (क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धांत — d कक्षकों का विपाटन)

 

• Depending on the geometry of the complex (octahedral, tetrahedral, square planar, etc.), the five originally degenerate d orbitals split into sets of different energies — for example, into t2g and eg sets in an octahedral field.

 

• This splitting explains key properties of coordination compounds such as their colour, magnetic behaviour (high-spin/low-spin complexes) and stability.

 

• CFT was developed by physicists Hans Bethe and John Hasbrouck van Vleck and was later extended (incorporating covalent bonding character) into Ligand Field Theory.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The crystal field splitting energy is denoted by the symbol Δ (delta), or specifically Δo for octahedral and Δt for tetrahedral complexes.

 

• Ligand Field Theory (LFT) builds upon CFT by incorporating some covalent character of the metal-ligand bond using molecular orbital concepts.

 

NOTE

 

• Ligand field theory (Option 2): A more advanced theory that combines crystal field theory with molecular orbital theory to include covalent bonding, but the specific description in the question (purely electrostatic splitting due to ligand field/geometry) matches CFT.

 

• Valence bond theory (Option 3): Explains bonding and geometry of complexes using hybridisation of metal orbitals, but does not directly explain d-orbital splitting.

 

• Molecular orbital theory (Option 4): A more comprehensive bonding theory involving combination of atomic orbitals into molecular orbitals, distinct from the specific electrostatic d-orbital splitting concept described.

question: The West Bengal government has launched 'Paray Shikshalaya’ programme. This initiative supports _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is open air classroom.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Paray Shikshalaya' (meaning "school in the neighbourhood") is an initiative of the West Bengal government that supports open-air/outdoor classrooms conducted in local neighbourhoods. (पाड়ায় শিক্ষালয় — खुली हवा में कक्षा)

 

• It was launched to help school children continue learning informally at the community level, especially in the context of prolonged school closures during the COVID-19 pandemic.

 

• Under this scheme, teachers and trained community volunteers conduct small, open-air classes in parks, courtyards, or other open community spaces close to students' homes, following health and safety protocols.

 

• The programme aimed to bridge learning gaps and prevent dropouts caused by extended school closures.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• West Bengal's Chief Minister is Mamata Banerjee.

 

• The scheme is implemented by the West Bengal School Education Department, in coordination with local panchayats and municipalities.

 

NOTE

 

• Financial assistance for girl child (Option 2): This describes schemes like Kanyashree Prakalpa, a separate West Bengal initiative, not Paray Shikshalaya.

 

• Blackboard distribution in every school (Option 3): Not the focus of this programme.

 

• Higher education for class 10th students (Option 4): Not related to Paray Shikshalaya, which targets community-level informal school-level learning.

question: Which Indian musician performed ‘Raga For Peace’ at the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize Concert in Oslo?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amjad Ali Khan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Amjad Ali Khan, the renowned sarod maestro, performed a composition titled 'Raga For Peace' along with his sons Amaan Ali Bangash and Ayaan Ali Bangash at the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize Concert held in Oslo, Norway. (अमजद अली खान — सरोद वादक, नोबेल शांति पुरस्कार समारोह)

 

• The concert was held to honour the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize laureates, India's Kailash Satyarthi and Pakistan's Malala Yousafzai, who jointly won the award for their work on children's and young people's rights.

 

• The performance was a tribute celebrating the shared theme of peace and harmony that the award recognised.

 

• Amjad Ali Khan belongs to the Senia Bangash gharana of sarod playing and has been a recipient of the Padma Vibhushan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kailash Satyarthi is an Indian child rights and education activist, founder of the Bachpan Bachao Andolan.

 

• Amjad Ali Khan has composed several ragas and has performed extensively across the world to promote Indian classical music.

 

NOTE

 

• Bahadur Khan (Option 1): A sarod player of an earlier generation (brother of Ali Akbar Khan), not the performer at the 2014 concert.

 

• Buddhadev Das Gupta (Option 3): A noted sarod player, but not the one who performed at the 2014 Nobel concert.

 

• Satyaki Banerjee (Option 4): Not associated with this event.

question: Who has been appointed as the chairman of Defence Research and Development Organisation and in August 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Samir V Kamat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr Samir V. Kamat was appointed as the Chairman of the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and Secretary, Department of Defence R&D, in August 2022. (समीर वी. कामत — DRDO अध्यक्ष)

 

• He succeeded Dr G. Satheesh Reddy, who completed his tenure as DRDO Chairman.

 

• Prior to this appointment, Dr Kamat served as the Director-General (Naval Systems and Materials) at DRDO and had earlier headed the Naval Materials Research Laboratory (NMRL).

 

• DRDO, headquartered in New Delhi, is India's premier agency for defence research, established in 1958.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• DRDO functions under the Ministry of Defence, Government of India, and operates a network of laboratories across the country.

 

• India's first Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), General Bipin Rawat, died in a helicopter crash in December 2021; General Anil Chauhan was later appointed as the second CDS in September 2022.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajiv Bahl (Option 1): Was appointed as the Director-General of the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), not DRDO.

 

• Anil Chouhan (Option 2): General Anil Chauhan was appointed Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) in September 2022, a different post from DRDO Chairman.

 

• Ranjit Rath (Option 4): Chairman and Managing Director of Oil India Limited (OIL), not related to DRDO.

question: An undifferentiated layer, ______, is present in between the ectoderm and the endoderm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mesoglea.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mesoglea is a gelatinous, largely acellular, undifferentiated layer found between the ectoderm (outer layer) and endoderm (inner layer) in diploblastic animals such as Cnidarians (Coelenterates) and Ctenophores. (मध्यजीवद्रव्य/मेसोग्लिया — बहिस्त्वचा और अंतस्त्वचा के बीच की परत)

 

• Unlike the true mesoderm found in triploblastic animals, the mesoglea is not a properly differentiated germ layer — it is a jelly-like, largely non-cellular matrix that provides structural support, especially in soft-bodied animals like jellyfish.

 

• It gives animals like jellyfish their characteristic gelatinous, semi-transparent, buoyant body structure.

 

• Organisms possessing only two germ layers (ectoderm and endoderm), with mesoglea in between, are called diploblastic animals, as opposed to triploblastic animals which have a true mesoderm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Examples of diploblastic (Cnidarian) animals include Hydra, jellyfish (Aurelia), sea anemones and corals.

 

• Triploblastic animals (with ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm), such as flatworms, annelids and chordates, are further classified based on the presence/absence of a body cavity (coelom) as acoelomate, pseudocoelomate, or coelomate.

 

NOTE

 

• Coeliea, Ectinoglea (Options 1 and 3): Not recognised biological terms.

 

• Acoelomea (Option 2): Not the correct term for the middle layer; "acoelomate" refers to animals lacking a true body cavity (coelom), a different concept from the mesoglea layer.

question: Developing place of settlement is called _________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Site.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In human geography, the "site" of a settlement refers to the actual physical land/location on which a settlement is built and develops — its ground-level characteristics such as terrain, water availability, drainage and soil. (साइट — बस्ती का भौतिक स्थान)

 

• Site is distinguished from "situation", which refers to the settlement's location relative to its surrounding region (e.g. nearby rivers, trade routes, other towns).

 

• Favourable site factors — such as flat land, availability of fresh water, defensibility, and fertile soil — have historically influenced where settlements originate and develop.

 

• As a settlement grows and matures over time on a given site, its layout, structures and population expand around this original physical location.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Settlements are broadly classified as rural and urban, and further by pattern as nucleated, linear, dispersed, etc.

 

• Common favourable site factors studied in geography include wet-point sites (near water), dry-point sites (avoiding flooding) and defensive sites (e.g. hilltops, river bends).

 

NOTE

 

• Home (Option 1): Refers to an individual dwelling, not the geographical concept of a settlement's location.

 

• Plain (Option 3): A landform type (flat, low-relief land), not a term describing the location/place of a settlement.

 

• Shelter (Option 4): Refers to a structure providing protection, not a geographical term for a settlement's site.

question: Which of the following is caused by exagenic force?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Crosion (Erosion).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Exogenic (exogenetic) forces are geomorphic forces that originate from outside the Earth's surface — mainly driven by the Sun's energy, gravity, and atmospheric/hydrological processes — and act to wear down and level the Earth's surface. (बहिर्जनिक बल — अपरदन)

 

• Erosion (printed as "Crosion" in the source, a typographical rendering of "Erosion") — the wearing away and removal of rock and soil material by agents such as running water, wind, glaciers and waves — is a classic example of a process driven by exogenic forces.

 

• Exogenic processes include weathering, erosion, transportation and deposition, and collectively work to reduce relief and level out landforms created by internal (endogenic) forces.

 

• In contrast, endogenic forces originate from within the Earth (driven by heat energy in the Earth's interior) and are responsible for building up landforms, such as mountain building, faulting and volcanic activity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Endogenic forces are broadly classified into diastrophic forces (slow, e.g. folding, faulting) and sudden forces (e.g. earthquakes, volcanic eruptions).

 

• Exogenic processes are also called gradational processes, since they gradually reduce relief through degradation (erosion) and aggradation (deposition).

 

NOTE

 

• Landslide (Option 2): Primarily driven by gravity acting on unstable slopes (mass wasting); commonly grouped separately from purely exogenic surface processes in standard classifications, and is not the intended answer here.

 

• Earthquake (Option 3): Caused by endogenic forces — sudden release of energy from within the Earth's crust along fault lines.

 

• Volcano (Option 4): Caused by endogenic forces — the movement of molten magma from within the Earth to the surface.

question: How many times has India hosted the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup (One Day)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As of this exam (December 2022), India had hosted (or co-hosted) the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup three times: in 1987, 1996, and 2011. (क्रिकेट विश्व कप — भारत की मेज़बानी तीन बार)

 

• 1987 World Cup: Co-hosted by India and Pakistan (won by Australia); it was the first World Cup held outside England.

 

• 1996 World Cup: Co-hosted by India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka (won by Sri Lanka).

 

• 2011 World Cup: Co-hosted by India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh; India won the tournament, defeating Sri Lanka in the final at the Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai, under captain MS Dhoni.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India subsequently hosted the World Cup for a fourth time (solely, not co-hosted) in 2023, which falls after this exam's time frame.

 

• India has won the ODI World Cup twice as of December 2022 — in 1983 (led by Kapil Dev) and 2011 (led by MS Dhoni).

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (2, 1, 4): Do not match the correct count of three hostings by India up to the time of this exam (1987, 1996, 2011).

question: The first match of IPL 2022 was played in_______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mumbai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The opening match of the Indian Premier League (IPL) 2022 season was played on 26 March 2022 at the Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai. (आईपीएल 2022 — पहला मैच, मुंबई)

 

• The first match was contested between Chennai Super Kings (CSK) and Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR), with KKR winning the match.

 

• IPL 2022 was the 15th season of the league and notably featured 10 teams for the first time, with the addition of two new franchises, Gujarat Titans and Lucknow Super Giants.

 

• Gujarat Titans, captained by Hardik Pandya, won the IPL 2022 title in their debut season, defeating Rajasthan Royals in the final.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The IPL 2022 final was played at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad.

 

• Jos Buttler (Rajasthan Royals) won the Orange Cap (highest run-scorer) and Yuzvendra Chahal (Rajasthan Royals) won the Purple Cap (highest wicket-taker) in IPL 2022.

 

NOTE

 

• Bengaluru (Option 1): Home venue of Royal Challengers Bangalore, but not the venue of the IPL 2022 opening match.

 

• Kolkata (Option 3): Home venue of Kolkata Knight Riders, but the opening match was played at Mumbai, not Kolkata.

 

• Lucknow (Option 4): Home venue of the new franchise Lucknow Super Giants, but not the venue of the season's first match.

question: In India initially HYVP was implemented in about how much area?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2 million hectares.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The High Yielding Varieties Programme (HYVP) was launched in India in 1966-67, as a key component of the Green Revolution, to introduce high-yielding seed varieties of wheat, rice, maize, jowar and bajra. (उच्च उपज किस्म कार्यक्रम — लगभग 2 मिलियन हेक्टेयर)

 

• It was initially implemented over an area of about 1.89 million hectares, commonly rounded off to approximately 2 million hectares, and was subsequently expanded significantly over the following years.

 

• The programme is closely associated with agricultural scientist Dr M. S. Swaminathan, regarded as the "Father of the Green Revolution in India", and with agronomist Norman Borlaug, who developed high-yielding wheat varieties.

 

• The HYVP led to a substantial increase in foodgrain production in India, particularly in states like Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Green Revolution in India is generally dated from the mid-1960s, coinciding with the Third Five-Year Plan period.

 

• The HYVP is also referred to as the New Agricultural Strategy.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (5, 3 and 4 million hectares): Do not match the historically recorded initial coverage of approximately 2 million hectares.

question: Which of the following greenhouse gases is most abundant in the atmosphere?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Water Vapour.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Water vapour (H₂O) is the most abundant greenhouse gas in Earth's atmosphere by concentration, and it contributes the largest share to the natural greenhouse effect. (जलवाष्प — सबसे प्रचुर ग्रीनहाउस गैस)

 

• Unlike carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases, the concentration of water vapour in the atmosphere is largely governed by natural processes (evaporation and precipitation) rather than direct human emissions, though warming increases atmospheric water vapour through a positive feedback loop.

 

• Other important greenhouse gases include carbon dioxide (CO₂), methane (CH₄), nitrous oxide (N₂O) and ozone (O₃), but all are present in far smaller concentrations than water vapour.

 

• The greenhouse effect caused by these gases is essential for maintaining Earth's habitable temperature, but excess concentrations of gases like CO₂ and methane (largely from human activity) are driving anthropogenic climate change.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is the greenhouse gas most significantly increased by human activities (fossil fuel combustion, deforestation) and is the primary focus of climate change mitigation efforts.

 

• Methane (CH₄) has a much higher global warming potential per molecule than CO₂ but is present in much smaller quantities.

 

NOTE

 

• Nitrous Oxide (Option 1): A potent greenhouse gas (from agricultural and industrial sources) but present in trace amounts compared to water vapour.

 

• Methane (Option 3): A significant greenhouse gas but far less abundant than water vapour.

 

• Carbon Oxide (Option 4): Likely refers to carbon dioxide/monoxide; also far less abundant in the atmosphere than water vapour.

question: Who among the following was the best-known Chahamana ruler?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prithviraja III.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Prithviraja III, popularly known as Prithviraj Chauhan, is the best-known ruler of the Chahamana (Chauhan) dynasty, which ruled over the Sapadalaksha region (present-day north-eastern Rajasthan and adjoining areas), with Ajmer and later Delhi as important centres. (पृथ्वीराज तृतीय — चाहमान/चौहान वंश के प्रसिद्ध शासक)

 

• He is most famous for defeating Muhammad of Ghor (Muizzuddin Muhammad Ghori) in the First Battle of Tarain (1191), but was subsequently defeated and killed by Ghori in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192).

 

• His court poet Chand Bardai composed the epic Prithviraj Raso, chronicling his life and exploits (though its historical accuracy is debated by historians).

 

• His defeat in 1192 is often regarded as a turning point that opened the way for the establishment of Turkic Muslim rule in northern India, eventually leading to the Delhi Sultanate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chahamanas were one of the "Agnivanshi" Rajput clans (along with the Pratiharas, Chalukyas/Solankis, and Paramaras) according to later Rajput tradition.

 

• Ajayaraja II, an earlier Chahamana ruler, is credited with founding the city of Ajmer.

 

NOTE

 

• Vigraharaja II (Option 2): An earlier Chahamana ruler, but far less prominent historically than Prithviraja III.

 

• Prithviraja I (Option 3): An earlier Chahamana ruler (11th century), not as famous as his descendant Prithviraja III.

 

• Vasudeva (Option 4): Not a well-known Chahamana ruler; the name is more commonly associated with other dynasties/contexts (e.g. the Kanva dynasty).

question: In which year was the Indian Parliamentary Group established?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1949.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Parliamentary Group (IPG) was established in 1949, prior to India formally becoming a Republic. (भारतीय संसदीय समूह — स्थापना 1949)

 

• The IPG serves as a link between the Parliament of India and parliaments/legislatures of other countries, and is also the national group affiliated to the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU).

 

• It works to promote a better understanding of parliamentary democracy and to facilitate the exchange of views and cooperation between Indian parliamentarians and their counterparts abroad.

 

• Its membership comprises members of both Houses of Parliament — the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is ex-officio the President of the Indian Parliamentary Group.

 

• The IPG's secretariat is housed within the Parliament of India Secretariat in New Delhi.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4 (1950, 1948, 1951): Do not match the year of establishment; the IPG was founded in 1949.

question: The government of India initiated the comprehensive family planning programme in the year ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1972.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• While India launched its National Family Planning Programme in 1952 (the first country in the world to do so), a reorganised and expanded "comprehensive" Family Planning Programme, integrating maternal and child health services and broader welfare measures, is dated to 1972. (परिवार नियोजन कार्यक्रम — व्यापक स्वरूप, 1972)

 

• The 1972 reorganisation broadened the scope of the programme beyond simple birth control targets to include a more holistic approach covering maternal and child health (MCH), nutrition and family welfare.

 

• The programme was later renamed the Family Welfare Programme in 1977, reflecting this broader, more comprehensive approach.

 

• Family planning in India has evolved through several phases, from a purely clinical approach in the 1950s to target-based approaches in later decades, and eventually to the target-free, need-based approach adopted from 1996 onwards.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's family planning programme has been implemented through successive Five-Year Plans, with significant policy shifts especially after the Emergency period (1975-77), when coercive sterilisation drives led to public backlash.

 

• The National Population Policy (NPP) 2000 set long-term demographic goals, including achieving population stabilisation by 2045.

 

NOTE

 

• 1960 (Option 1): Predates the reorganisation into a comprehensive programme.

 

• 1991 (Option 2) and 1982 (Option 4): Do not correspond to the year the programme was made comprehensive; these do not match the standard reference year of 1972.

question: Which of the following revolts was led by Kanhu and Sidhu?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Santhal Revolt.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Santhal Revolt (Santhal Hool) of 1855-56 was led by the brothers Sidhu Murmu and Kanhu Murmu, along with their siblings Chand and Bhairav, and sisters Phulo and Jhano. (संथाल विद्रोह — सिद्धू और कान्हू)

 

• The revolt broke out in the Rajmahal Hills/Santhal Parganas region (present-day Jharkhand) against exploitation by zamindars, moneylenders (mahajans) and the oppressive British colonial administration.

 

• The rebellion led the British to create the separate district of the Santhal Parganas in 1855 to administer the region under distinct regulations.

 

• The Santhal Hool is regarded as one of the earliest large-scale armed uprisings against British rule, predating the Revolt of 1857.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• 30 June is observed as Hul Diwas (Santhal Hul Day) in Jharkhand to commemorate the revolt.

 

• Both Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu were eventually captured and executed by the British.

 

NOTE

 

• Bheel Revolt (Option 1): An early 19th-century uprising by the Bhil tribal community, notably led by figures like Sewaram in Khandesh, unrelated to Sidhu and Kanhu.

 

• Khasi Revolt (Option 2): Led by U Tirot Sing against the British in the Khasi Hills (Meghalaya) in 1829-33.

 

• Munda Revolt (Option 3): Led by Birsa Munda in the Chotanagpur region (1899-1900), also known as the Ulgulan.

question: Identify an example of diploblastic animals.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Coelenterates.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Diploblastic animals are those whose embryonic body develops from only two germ layers — an outer ectoderm and an inner endoderm — with an undifferentiated, jelly-like mesoglea in between (rather than a true mesoderm). (द्विकोरकी प्राणी — सिलेंट्रेटा/निडारिया)

 

• Coelenterates (Cnidaria), such as Hydra, jellyfish, sea anemones and corals, are classic examples of diploblastic animals.

 

• Ctenophores (comb jellies) are also diploblastic, along with Cnidarians, together forming the diploblastic grade of animal organisation.

 

• Diploblastic animals typically show radial symmetry, in contrast to triploblastic animals, which have three germ layers (adding mesoderm) and generally show bilateral symmetry.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Coelenterates show two basic body forms: a sessile polyp (e.g. Hydra) and a free-swimming medusa (e.g. jellyfish).

 

• Some coelenterates, like corals, secrete a calcium carbonate skeleton and are vital in the formation of coral reefs.

 

NOTE

 

• Platyhelminthes (Option 1): Flatworms; these are triploblastic acoelomate animals (e.g. Planaria, tapeworms), not diploblastic.

 

• Arachnids (Option 2): Belong to phylum Arthropoda; they are triploblastic coelomate animals.

 

• Chordates (Option 3): Include vertebrates and related groups; they are triploblastic coelomate animals.
